core.title: Declare abstract Gherkin narrative in every acceptance given/when/then section
core.given: An acceptance document with given/when/then sections exists or is being written.
core.when: You author, edit or review that acceptance.
core.then: Every section must carry all three REQUIRED abstract narrative fields: given.abstract (non-empty list of strings, each item a single precondition/setup state), when.abstract (string of at least 5 characters, present tense, clear actor and action), then.abstract (non-empty list of strings, each item a single observable outcome).
prefer: Keep the abstract narrative fields alongside the structured machine fields in the same section: abstract for stakeholders (Gherkin), structured for machines (test generation).
Use identity.purpose as the scenario name; a separate top-level name is not needed.
avoid: Omitting any abstract field or leaving given/then lists empty.
Bundling several preconditions or outcomes into one item.
Replacing structured machine fields with the narrative (they coexist).
Placeholder text that passes length/count checks without describing a real state, action or outcome.
core.why: Abstract Gherkin narrative makes each acceptance readable by stakeholders while structured fields stay machine-consumable for test generation.
evidence: Every acceptance section has given.abstract as array[str] with minItems 1, and each item states a single precondition/setup state (required, not optional).
Every acceptance section has when.abstract as str with minLength 5, present tense, with a clear actor and action.
Every acceptance section has then.abstract as array[str] with minItems 1, each item a single observable outcome.
identity.purpose serves as the scenario name; a separate top-level name is unnecessary (its presence is not itself a violation).
verification: A schema check over the abstract narrative fields of every acceptance document: presence, type and size are mechanical (given.abstract and then.abstract: array[str] with minItems 1; when.abstract: str with minLength 5, REQUIRED); item atomicity (single precondition / single outcome), present tense and clear actor/action are mandatory but LLM-judged.

Violations are reported as a missing or malformed abstract field; the exact detector, validator and finding ids of this rule are realization details. No such detector exists yet in the reference realization (needs_new_observer).

Scope: the acceptance document itself, however it is reached; artifacts with no acceptance given/when/then sections and code or tests generated from acceptances are out of scope. How a stack recognizes acceptance documents is stack data from the profile's acceptance role: the concrete acceptance file kind, plus a path pattern only when the stack identifies them by location — a stack that specifies no path pattern does not get one invented for it.

fires: A planner authors a new acceptance whose given/when/then sections carry only structured machine fields and no abstract narrative.
A planner edits an acceptance (in any part, e.g. identity metadata) whose then.abstract is an empty list.
An existing acceptance under review has when.abstract as a list or as a string shorter than 5 characters.
An acceptance's given.abstract item bundles several preconditions into one line.
doesNotFire: Plan artifacts, product slices or other documents that contain no acceptance given/when/then sections.
Code or test files produced from acceptances (the rule governs the acceptance document, not generated tests).

profileRequirements.meaning: The concrete artifact kinds that play the acceptance-test role; 'acceptance' is the kind whose given/when/then sections this rule's activation fact and schema check target. Recognition policy beyond this kind list (e.g. by an acceptance path pattern) belongs to the stack's role assignment, and bun.json defers it without naming a pattern.

neutralityNotes: The abstract-field schema itself (given.abstract, when.abstract, then.abstract, identity.purpose, minItems 1, minLength 5, array[str]/str types) belongs to the stack-neutral ATDD acceptance-document format and was kept verbatim in the core; no stack, runtime, language or path is named. Three things could not be made neutral and stay with the Bun realization: (1) the rule's finding ids (acceptance.abstract-field-missing / -malformed) and the note that no such detector exists yet, (2) the project-specific verifier examples (appendix.convention.yaml, wagon manifest, resolver/URN), and (3) the note's 'acceptance path pattern' recognition mechanism, which names no concrete pattern. The word "wagons" in activation.doesNotFire[0] (ATDD-Bun's bounded product slice) was neutralized to "product slices". Profile data: bun.json supplies exactly one concrete kind for the acceptance role — "acceptance" (activation.facts[0].values) — which populates roles.acceptance_test.kinds; it defers any path-based recognition without specifying a pattern, so roles.acceptance_test.path is deliberately not populated and that deferral is stated in core:verification rather than filled with an invented glob. No new vocabulary key was needed.
